newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Deng Xiaoping sends condolences to comrade.
newsitem.headline: China's Deng Xiaoping sends condolences to comrade.

text.p: China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, whose activities are now rarely mentioned in the Chinese media, has sent his condolences to the family of late foreign trade minister Li Qiang.

The People's Daily, mouthpiece of the Communist Party, on Thursday listed Deng in second place after Communist Party boss and state president Jiang Zemin in a list of people who sent their condolences to Li's family.
It did not say whether Deng had offered condolences in person.
Deng, 92, no longer holds any office but is believed to remain highly influential. He has not been seen in public since early 1994.

Deng's health is a matter of intense speculation in China, Hong Kong and the Asian region because his death is expected to trigger a scramble for power among those eager to succeed him as de facto emperor of the world's most populous nation.
The official line is that he is in good health for a man of his age.
Li was cremated on Wednesday. He died in Beijing on September 29 at the age of 91.
Other leaders, including Premier Li Peng, also sent their condolences to the family, the newspaper said.
